channel.title: Economy
channel.description: Find the latest economic news, current events and headlines, as well as blogs and video from CNBC.com.

item.title: Men are losing ground in the labor market. Here's why
item.description: Women outnumbered men in the workforce for eight straight months as of September, according to one analysis.

item.title: Labor market faltered in September as jobs increased by just 29,000, unemployment rate rose to 4.2%
item.description: Nonfarm payrolls rose by just 29,000 in September, well below the 84,000 forecast, and the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said.

item.title: The September jobs report will be released Friday. Here's what to expect
item.description: Wall Street is looking for job growth of 84,000 to close out the summer.

item.title: Fed’s preferred gauge showed core inflation at 3.0% in August, much lighter than expected
item.description: The personal consumption expenditures price index was projected to show an annual gain of 3.7% on headline and 3.3% for core, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

item.title: Private sector jobs rose by 90,000 in September, better than expected, ADP reports
item.description: Private job creation picked up in September after a brief slowdown.

item.title: The Fed's main inflation measure will be released Wednesday. Here's what to expect
item.description: Data is expected to show ongoing price pressures and consumers who nevertheless continue to spend.

item.title: Consumer optimism slides to lowest since 2014 as fears escalate over rising prices and jobs
item.description: The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index tumbled to 81.9, a decline of 6.7 points and a reading well below the forecast for 89.

item.title: America's Canadian import restrictions come into force. Here are the products barred from entry
item.description: President Donald Trump says he expects Ottawa to concede to its demands on trade in the coming weeks, but Canadian officials insist they won't sign a bad deal.

item.title: Australia says more hikes not off the table after raising rates to 15-year high
item.description: The hike of 25 basis points was in line with expectations by economists polled by Reuters.

item.title: China posts weakest industrial profit growth this year, expanding 4.2% in August
item.description: Economists expect Beijing to lean harder on stimulus to stabilize corporate profitability, as consolidation accelerates in sectors facing sluggish demand and fierce competition.

item.title: China saw 'surprise' jump in U.S. orders ahead of Trump-Xi summit, private survey shows
item.description: A private survey shows a rebound in China's exports to the U.S. as companies position for continued stability between the world's two largest economies.

item.title: Surging Treasury yields pose a brand new problem for Kevin Warsh and the Fed
item.description: Markets expect the central bank will take a firmer hand on inflation. It's not that easy.

item.title: Global debt tops $365 trillion as economists sound alarm over 'vicious cycle'
item.description: More is being paid out by advanced economies in debt interest than the whole world spends on AI, defense or clean technology.

item.title: Switzerland is keeping rates at 0% — for now
item.description: The Swiss National Bank held rates at 0% as low inflation and a strong franc enable it to diverge from other central banks, though markets expect hikes ahead.

item.title: France's fresh budget battle threatens to topple another government
item.description: Time is not on the side of French government bonds, strategists have warned, as the nation's deficit balloons.

item.title: World heads into food crises 'blind' as U.S. aid cuts squeeze UN food agency, experts warn
item.description: Climate shocks, conflict and a global fuel crisis, on top of surging interest rates and donor cuts, leave agencies less able to help those facing higher food prices.

item.title: Here's what happens to the economy when Treasury yields soar like they are now
item.description: Government debt costs leaped higher Wednesday, the product of multiple factors.

item.title: France’s wine production nears a 70-year low, leaving winemakers with tough choices
item.description: As the French wine industry reaches a crisis point, key players are considering new markets, products and generations.

item.title: Consumer sentiment is in the dumps despite a solid economy. Goldman Sachs blames 'lower happiness'
item.description: Goldman economist Joseph Briggs said broader pessimism in society may be contributing to struggling consumer sentiment even as the economy chugs along.

item.title: Why Japan’s markets flipped the usual script after central bank rate hike
item.description: The yen weakened past 157 against the dollar, the yield on the 10-year Japanese Government Bond slipped, while the Nikkei 225 gained 1.5%.

item.title: Bank of England defies Fed’s rate-hike lead, leaving rates unchanged
item.description: The Bank of England kept rates steady Thursday, even after U.K. inflation rose to 3.1% and energy costs put pressure on prices.

item.title: 'Science fiction': Transport companies — the backbone of economy — are sounding alarm on fuel prices
item.description: Prices for diesel, the fuel type used to power trucks and trains, came in at an all-time high of $6.31 per gallon on Wednesday.

item.title: Consumers hit by one-two punch of oil and rates from Iran war. The estimated bill is $1,700 per household
item.description: Rising oil prices and Treasury yields are lifting energy and borrowing costs for U.S. households, pushing consumers to draw more heavily on savings.

item.title: UK inflation jumps to 3.1% as energy costs soar
item.description: The reading comes a day before the Bank of England updates its monetary policy.

item.title: Indonesia's new finance minister faces an uphill battle on fiscal credibility
item.description: Nazara, sworn in hours after Purbaya's dismissal, spent seven years as deputy finance minister and led the ministry's fiscal policy agency from 2015 to 2019.

item.title: Why de-dollarization discussions are more talk, less action
item.description: BRICS leaders have asserted the need to use local currencies in intra-BRICS trade to cut dependency on dollar.

item.title: Counting the votes: Warsh faces a tough battle as the Fed girds for expected interest rate hike
item.description: Traders were pricing in a better than 92% probability of a rate increase, as well as a more than 75% chance for another one in December.

item.title: Inflation is outpacing wage growth again, squeezing Americans’ paychecks
item.description: In August, consumer prices rose 3.4% over the past year while wages increased just 3.1%.

item.title: Consumer outlook plunges in September as inflation outlook worsens
item.description: The survey's headline index hit a level of 47.8, down 7.5% from the August reading and off 13.2% from a year ago.

item.title: Record U.S. cyclosporiasis outbreak is over, CDC says
item.description: The largest outbreak, linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms, sickened more than 12,000 people.
